 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Dwyane Wade has hit back at Rudy Gobert's critics, insisting the Minnesota Timberwolves center deserves far more recognition. The three-time NBA champion believes basketball fans often focus on the wrong aspects of Gobert's game instead of appreciating his enormous defensive impact. 
 Gobert has had a difficult start to the season on offense, averaging just 8.2 points per game compared to 10.9 last campaign. His field goal percentage has also dropped from 68.2% to 46.8%, but scoring has never been the Frenchman's greatest strength.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The 34-year-old remains an important presence on the boards, averaging 11.7 rebounds per game, while his defense continues to make him one of Minnesota's most valuable players. The Timberwolves currently have the lowest defensive rating in the NBA at 104.1.
 Wade has been particularly impressed by how Gobert can influence an entire defensive system , having watched him closely during his time with the Utah Jazz. Speaking about the center, the former Miami Heat star explained why he believes the criticism directed towards him is often misplaced.
 "People like to talk a lot about Rudy because we see highlights they like to show when he fumbled the ball, when someone dunks on him, or some things he gets into physically that may not be what Rudy is known for, right? When I watched Rudy, when I got to Utah, I realized that Rudy is an entire defense by himself," Wade said.
 Wade also pointed to the defensive support Gobert receives from his teammates, including Jaden McDaniels and Ayo Dosunmu, but insisted the former Jazz big man remains the foundation of Minnesota's success. He believes opponents have to completely change their approach when they face the four-time Defensive Player of the Year.
 Wade continued: "Put some respect on what he does great. Everybody is always talking about what someone does not do, what their talent isn't. What is he doing? Every year his team is one of the top teams in defense.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "And you know what that is? That's why this team has been in the Western Conference Finals the last few years, because their calling card is defense, and that man right there is the anchor of it all."
 Minnesota have made an impressive start to the campaign, sitting at 10-4 despite Anthony Edwards dealing with injury problems lately . Gobert's defensive influence has been a major reason for their strong form, and Wade believes his contribution deserves considerably more appreciation.
